request: 아주 좋아 또 한 5개정도 알아봐줘 제작할꺼
scope: Five researched production candidates only. No production, TTS, rendering, scheduling, upload or next-video authorization inferred from this research request.

comparison.coverage: Compared current local worklist and 70 public titles captured on October 24. No new exhaustive channel transcript audit or worldwide uniqueness claim.

recommendationReason: Material changes and their chain reactions produce a clear opening, and a small grid can expose the underlying rule without relying on mathematical prerequisites. Viewfinder has the strongest alternate visual reveal but requires more complex mesh-cutting demonstration work.

candidates.title: 불붙은 픽셀 하나가 동굴을 태우는 이유
candidates.technique: Pixel-based material simulation / 픽셀 기반 물질 시뮬레이션

primarySources.readScope: Pixel-based physics and FAQ: each pixel has a material, water flows, gas rises, sand piles up, simplified reactions/electricity/thermodynamics; in-house Falling Everything Engine.
Indexed official abstract identifies falling-sand simulation and destructible rigid-body integration. Full presentation was unavailable because Vault redirected to maintenance; not claimed watched.

candidates.verifiedClaim: The world uses simulated material pixels with liquid, gas, granular and reaction behavior, alongside rigid bodies.
visualPlan: Actual gameplay shows a clearly identifiable ignition and material reaction
Zoom to our simplified material grid with cells labeled oil, water and empty space
Change only the material surrounding the heat source and compare the result
Return to the corresponding game reaction
limits: Our teaching grid is an illustration, not recovered game internals.
Do not claim every pixel is a separate rigid-body object or that inactive world cells are updated every frame.
Verify the chosen exact ignition/reaction in independent footage before writing its narration.
candidates.overlapAssessment: Distinct from the captured generic destruction-effects title: emphasize simulated materials and reactions, not pre-broken meshes.
candidates.productionStatus: candidate-only; independent FHD footage and usage rights not yet secured

candidates.title: 사진을 들이댔더니 진짜 길이 생겼다?
candidates.technique: Runtime mesh slicing / 런타임 메시 절단

primarySources.kind: Direct interview with game director Matt Stark
primarySources.readScope: Full interview including prototype, photo physicality, single-frame mesh changes and Jacob's mesh-slicing optimization.

candidates.verifiedClaim: Taking and placing photographs modifies many meshes within one frame; the developer explicitly identifies optimized mesh-slicing code.
visualPlan: Actual photograph creates a walkable route across a gap
Show the same photo placement from an observer camera
Our demonstration exposes a clipping volume and the resulting cut geometry
Return to walking on the newly placed route
limits: The interview verifies mesh slicing, not every detail of serialization or clipping implementation.
Do not claim arbitrary external photographs are reconstructed by AI.
Source clips remain research-reference-only; acquire separate gameplay for the cut.
candidates.overlapAssessment: Different from Superliminal's size/distance relationship and Portal's second-camera rendering: focus on persistent geometry modification.
candidates.productionStatus: candidate-only; exact traversal footage, rights and a faithful simplified mesh demo remain to be prepared

candidates.title: 이 고양이 몸속에는 공 두 개가 있다?
candidates.technique: Procedural animation / 절차적 애니메이션; constrained body chunks / 거리 제약을 둔 몸체 구성 요소

primarySources.kind: Unity interview with Videocult and Akupara developers
primarySources.readScope: Animating the slugcat and adjacent implementation section: two spherical chunks at fixed distance; cosmetic limbs and tail animate procedurally; script-generated creature structures.

primarySources.kind: Joar Jakobsson and James Therrien GDC 2016 presentation
primarySources.readScope: Official talk identity and abstract; not claimed fully watched in this research pass.

candidates.verifiedClaim: The slugcat's base consists of two spherical chunks held at a fixed distance, with procedurally animated visual limbs and tail on top.
visualPlan: Actual slugcat tumbles or squeezes through a tunnel
Fade the visible body into our two-body explanation while preserving the same motion
Show the fixed-distance constraint as one body turns around the other
Restore limbs/tail and compare the recognizable result
limits: The two-chunk structure describes the slugcat; do not apply it to every creature.
Do not imply all animation or all collision consists exclusively of these two spheres.
Our debug shapes are a reconstruction and must not be presented as extracted game data.
candidates.overlapAssessment: Adjacent to the reference channel's stair IK topic, but a different mechanism and reveal: whole-body physical representation rather than foot placement. Avoid a generic IK lesson.
candidates.productionStatus: candidate-only; actual movement footage and rights remain unverified

candidates.title: 점프만 해도 우주로? 중력 공식을 바꾼 게임
candidates.technique: Gravity falloff / 중력 감쇠; inverse-square law / 역제곱 법칙

primarySources.kind: Direct interviews with Alex Beachum and Logan Ver Hoef
primarySources.readScope: Sum of all spheres: small planets made inverse-square gravity fall too quickly; early prototype reached escape velocity too easily; planetary gravity uses a more linear decrease while the sun retains inverse-square behavior.

candidates.verifiedClaim: The developers changed planetary gravity falloff because inverse-square gravity on their small planets made escape velocity too easy to reach. The article separately specifies the sun's inverse-square behavior.
visualPlan: Actual game shows a normal jump on a small curved planet
Same-size planet and same launch speed in our A/B demonstration
Compare rapidly weakening inverse-square gravity against a labeled illustrative slower falloff
Return to how the adopted design keeps tiny-planet traversal playable
limits: Headline question concerns the design problem, not a claim that the released game normally ejects the player on every jump.
Do not present an invented numeric formula, strength, radius or trajectory as the actual game implementation.
Distinguish planetary behavior from the sun and avoid an unrelated universal gravity lesson.
candidates.overlapAssessment: Different from a generic asymmetric platformer jump: focus on gravity varying with distance from a tiny planet and the developer's specific substitution.
candidates.productionStatus: candidate-only; actual jump capture and rights remain unverified

candidates.title: 색은 두 개인데 그림자는 어떻게 만들까?

primarySources.kind: Lucas Pope's original development log mirrored on his own site
primarySources.readScope: Dithering Process and stabilization discussion: 8-bit grayscale converted to 1-bit by pattern thresholds, Bayer/blue-noise patterns, swimming pixels under motion, mapping experiments. Later implementation must be read in full before fixing the final stabilization algorithm in a script.
Entire technical narrative: two colors, outlines, Bayer versus blue noise, fullscreen discomfort, camera-aware pattern improvement and 800x450 internal final resolution.

candidates.verifiedClaim: Dither patterns distribute two pixel colors to suggest intermediate shades. Camera motion made patterns uncomfortable; the developer adjusted how patterns relate to the 3D camera to reduce flicker.
visualPlan: Actual ship interior with readable light and shadow
Magnify a patch to reveal only two colors
Change the distribution of the two colors to show perceived gray
Brief same-camera demonstration of unstable and stabilized pattern, then real gameplay
limits: Two colors need not literally be black and white for every selectable palette.
Do not describe the game's entire internal pipeline as one bit: the devlog identifies intermediate grayscale rendering.
Use a genuine 1080p-or-higher recording of the intentionally low-resolution game, never upscale a low-resolution downloaded video.
Avoid claiming that one pattern completely removes all shimmer.
candidates.overlapAssessment: Related to pixel-art palette topics but focuses on 3D shading and temporal readability, not palette indexing or file compression.
candidates.productionStatus: candidate-only; independent FHD footage and rights remain unverified
